reason: The rover needs driven wheels, so joining the wheels to the gearmotors is a useful start.

reaction: The explanation of the speed-and-force tradeoff was useful.
reason: The ball caster should support the deck while allowing the driven wheels to steer it.
expectation: I expect the caster to be fitted to the rover deck, ready for the drive assembly.

reason: Use the only offered combination to test whether the rover responds to the remote.

effect: The raised-wheel test confirmed that the remote controls the drives independently; the chapter goal is complete, though the rover does not have a pen yet.
reaction: Testing safely in the jig made the assembly feel purposeful, and the distinction between battery energy and radio instructions was clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the receiver and motor driver clarified how separate wheel control makes steering possible.

leastWorthwhile.text: The battery and switch fittings were straightforward but felt like routine assembly.

surprise.text: The free-turning caster and different wheel speeds allow steering without a steering axle.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though several fittings were predictable and offered little meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the tested rover draws and delivers invitations; the steering mechanism was interesting, although the assembly became repetitive.
